title: The Krull Galois group as the limit of finite Galois groups
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and let $\Omega/K$ be a Galois field extension, meaning an algebraic, normal and separable field extension [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Equip $\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K)$ with its Krull topology. For each finite Galois intermediate field $L$ of $\Omega/K$, give $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ its discrete topology, with restriction as transition maps. The partially ordered set of finite Galois intermediate fields, ordered by inclusion, is nonempty and directed. Then the restriction map
$$
\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K)\longrightarrow\varprojlim_{L/K\ \mathrm{finite\ Galois}}\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)
$$
is an isomorphism of topological groups, where the inverse limit has its subspace topology in the product of finite discrete groups.

source.place: Tag 0BU2 (lemma-infinite-galois-limit), group-limit clause; Mathlib FieldTheory/Galois/Profinite.lean, InfiniteGalois.continuousMulEquivToLimit, lines 323-327; the nonempty directed indexing uses FiniteGaloisIntermediateField.instLattice and instOrderBot, Mathlib/FieldTheory/Galois/GaloisClosure.lean:92-97.
